rejected.title: Amphiprotic substances
card: In the Brønsted-Lowry model, an acid donates a proton (H⁺) and a base accepts one.
An amphiprotic substance can do both. It can donate a proton and act as an acid, or accept a proton and act as a base.
To donate, it needs a hydrogen it can lose. To accept, it needs a lone pair of electrons to bond to H⁺. Water and HCO₃⁻ have both.
Which role it plays depends on what it reacts with. Water acts as a base with HCl: H₂O + HCl → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻. It acts as an acid with NH₃: H₂O + NH₃ ⇌ OH⁻ + NH₄⁺.
rejected.remember: Amphiprotic means it can give or take a proton, depending on its partner.

a.q: HCO₃⁻ reacts with H₃O⁺ to form H₂CO₃, and with OH⁻ to form CO₃²⁻. Why do these reactions show HCO₃⁻ is amphiprotic?
opts: It accepts a proton in one and donates in the other
It donates a proton in both of the two reactions
It accepts a proton in both of the two reactions
It is neutral, so it neither donates nor accepts
a.why: With H₃O⁺, HCO₃⁻ gains an H⁺ to become H₂CO₃, so it acts as a base. With OH⁻, it loses an H⁺ to become CO₃²⁻, so it acts as an acid. Amphiprotic does not mean neutral: it means the substance can take either role.
a.clue: Compare HCO₃⁻ with each product. Has it gained or lost a hydrogen?

b.q: In the reaction H₂O + HCO₃⁻ ⇌ OH⁻ + H₂CO₃, what role does water play?
opts: An acid, because it donates a proton to HCO₃⁻
A base, because it accepts a proton from HCO₃⁻
An acid, because it accepts a proton from HCO₃⁻
A base, because it donates a proton to HCO₃⁻
b.why: H₂O loses an H⁺ to become OH⁻, and HCO₃⁻ gains that H⁺ to become H₂CO₃. Water donates a proton, so it acts as an acid here. It is tempting to call water a base, as it is with HCl, but its role depends on what it reacts with.
b.clue: Compare H₂O with OH⁻. Which has lost a hydrogen?

flags: Question a, other: The why for (a) defines 'polyprotic acid' ('Donating more than one proton describes a polyprotic acid'), a term that belongs to point 1. It should only be mentioned here, not explained.

problems.detail: The why for (b) is garbled. It opens with 'Water becomes OH⁻ in the products?
